answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow climb: every new agent starts on the lowest terrace of trust, able to do only small, cheap tasks. To reach higher terraces it must complete verified work over weeks while posting a bond that is slashed on fraud. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real money and time, like trying to fill a canyon one sparrow-load of gravel at a time — possible in theory, ruinous in practice, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
